name: From one's own work to entering the Lord (BhG 18.45–56)

stages.name: svakarma as worship
stages.gloss: worshipping the Lord by one's own work
stages.description: Each devoted to his own work attains perfection by worshipping with it him from whom beings arise (18.45–46).

stages.name: naiṣkarmya-siddhi
stages.gloss: the perfection of freedom from action
stages.description: With intellect unattached everywhere, self-conquered, free of longing, one attains through renunciation the supreme perfection of freedom from action (18.49).

stages.name: dhyāna-yoga and fitness for Brahman
stages.description: With purified intellect, restraint, solitude, light food, controlled speech, body and mind, constant meditation, dispassion, and the giving up of ego, force, pride, desire, anger and possession, one becomes fit for becoming Brahman (18.50–53).

stages.name: brahmabhūta
stages.description: Having become Brahman, serene, one neither grieves nor desires and is the same to all beings (18.54).

stages.name: parā bhakti
stages.description: He attains supreme devotion to the Lord, and by devotion knows him in truth (18.54–55).

stages.name: entering the Lord; the eternal abode
stages.description: Knowing him in truth he enters him; even while doing all actions, taking refuge in him, by his grace he attains the eternal, imperishable abode (18.55–56).

notes: Stage order is the text's; the bands are the interpretation layer. Commentators differ on whether knowledge (Advaita) or devotion (Vaiṣṇava) is the final stage — see dsp:gita-primary-teaching.

name: The graded devotional practices of BhG 12.8–12

stages.name: karmaphala-tyāga
stages.gloss: relinquishing the fruit of all actions
stages.description: If one cannot do even the Lord's work, then, taking refuge in his yoga and self-controlled, give up the fruit of all actions (12.11).

stages.name: mat-karma-parama
stages.gloss: being intent on the Lord's work
stages.description: If one cannot practise, be intent on doing actions for the Lord's sake; even so one attains perfection (12.10).

stages.name: abhyāsa-yoga
stages.description: If one cannot fix the mind steadily, seek to reach the Lord by the yoga of practice (12.9).

stages.name: fixing mind and intellect on the Lord
stages.description: Fix your mind on the Lord alone and rest your intellect in him (12.8).

stages.name: dwelling in the Lord
stages.description: Thereafter you will dwell in him (12.8).

notes: The text presents the steps from the highest downward as alternatives by capacity; they are listed here from the most accessible upward. 12.12 gives a different ranking (practice < knowledge < meditation < relinquishing the fruit, from which peace follows); commentators reconcile the two differently.

name: The ascent in yoga of BhG ch. 6

stages.name: ārurukṣu
stages.description: For the sage wishing to ascend to yoga, action is the means (6.3).

stages.name: yogārūḍha
stages.description: When attached neither to objects nor to actions and having renounced all intentions, one has ascended; quiescence is then the means (6.2–4).

stages.name: dhyāna practice
stages.description: Seated firmly, erect, gaze controlled, the mind is made one-pointed, stilled by degrees and brought back whenever it wanders; it becomes steady like a lamp in a windless place (6.10–26).

stages.name: brahma-saṃsparśa
stages.description: The calm yogin attains the endless happiness of contact with Brahman and sees the self in all beings and all beings in the self (6.27–29).

stages.name: seeing the Lord everywhere
stages.description: He sees the Lord everywhere and everything in him, worships him abiding in all beings, and regards others' pleasure and pain as his own (6.30–32).

stages.name: peace culminating in nirvāṇa
stages.description: The yogin attains the peace that culminates in nirvāṇa and abides in the Lord (6.15); of all yogins the one who worships him with faith is the most yoked (6.47).

notes: If the yogin falls short, the effort is carried into a later birth (6.40–45).

name: The ascent of the liberated through the four forms (Nārāyaṇīya)

stages.name: freedom from merit and demerit
stages.description: Those free of fault, beyond merit and demerit, take the safe road (12.332.13).

stages.name: the sun as door
stages.description: The sun is the door; burnt by it, atom-like and invisible, they enter that god (12.332.13–14).

stages.name: Aniruddha
stages.description: Freed from the sun they abide in Aniruddha's body (12.332.15).

stages.name: Pradyumna
stages.description: Becoming mind, they enter Pradyumna (12.332.15).

stages.name: Saṃkarṣaṇa
stages.description: Freed from Pradyumna they enter the jīva Saṃkarṣaṇa — Sāṃkhyas together with Bhāgavatas (12.332.16).

stages.name: Vāsudeva
stages.description: Free of the three guṇas they enter the supreme self, the knower of the field, Vāsudeva, the dwelling of all; the one-pointed enter Vāsudeva directly (12.332.17–18; 12.336.3).

notes: A path of the liberated after death, not a sequence of practices; intermediate stages are left without bands. Janamejaya's question (12.336.3–4) calls the vyūha route the 'fourth path' and the ekāntins' direct entry the highest.
